note: Frozen parameter logic. Each entry describes what backend/app/parameters/*.py actually does. Every parameter is scored by the model from its curated data; `dedicated_llm_pass` marks the handlers that additionally run their own classification pass before scoring, and tools/build_parameter_workbook.py re-validates that flag against the handler source so it cannot drift.

TECH-01.name: AI crawler permissions
TECH-01.definition: Whether robots.txt actually lets the major AI crawlers in. If GPTBot, ClaudeBot or PerplexityBot are disallowed, the site cannot be read or cited by those assistants however good its content is.
TECH-01.metric_brief: Fetch robots.txt once per scan and evaluate the Allow/Disallow rules for five named AI crawlers at the site root, falling back to the wildcard group where no bot-specific group exists. Score is the share of those crawlers that are allowed. UNKNOWN if robots.txt cannot be fetched or fails to parse.
TECH-01.metric:
Fetch /robots.txt once per scan and parse it with Protego. For each of the five AI crawlers (GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, PerplexityBot) evaluate the Allow/Disallow rules for path "/", falling back to the wildcard group when no bot-specific group exists.
Score = allowed bots / bots with a definite ALLOWED-or-BLOCKED decision x 100.
UNKNOWN if robots.txt cannot be fetched, or if it is non-empty but fails to parse.
TECH-01.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. robots.txt is a formal grammar with one correct interpretation, and Protego implements it. A language model would add latency, cost and run-to-run variation to a question that already has an exact, verifiable answer.

TECH-02.name: No CDN/firewall blocking AI crawlers
TECH-02.definition: Whether the CDN or firewall blocks AI crawlers even when robots.txt permits them. A bot-specific 403 or a stripped-down response is a silent block: permission is granted on paper but the content never reaches the assistant.
TECH-02.metric_brief: Fetch the homepage once with a browser user-agent to set a baseline, then once per AI crawler user-agent. A crawler counts as blocked on HTTP 403, 406 or 429, or when its response body is under 20% of the baseline. Score is the share of the five crawlers not blocked.
TECH-02.metric:
Fetch the homepage once with a normal browser user-agent to establish a baseline response size, then fetch it again once per AI-crawler user-agent. A bot counts as blocked if it receives HTTP 403, 406 or 429, or if its response body is under 20% of the baseline size (content starvation) while the baseline itself exceeded 500 bytes.
Score = (5 - blocked bots) / 5 x 100.   Confidence 0.6.
TECH-02.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. The evidence is HTTP status codes and response byte counts, both measured directly. Confidence is held at 0.6 because a site legitimately serving different content per user-agent is indistinguishable from a block by size alone - a data limitation, not a judgment an LLM could resolve.

TECH-03.name: llms.txt present, accurate and current
TECH-03.definition: Whether the site publishes an /llms.txt file, the emerging convention for telling AI systems which pages matter and how to use them. Its presence, working links and a visible date signal a site actively curated for AI consumption.
TECH-03.metric_brief: Fetch /llms.txt. Missing or empty scores 0. Otherwise 40 base, plus 20 for real content, up to 20 for the share of sampled markdown links that resolve, and 20 for a date appearing anywhere in the file. Capped at 100.
TECH-03.metric:
Fetch /llms.txt. Missing or empty gives 0. Otherwise: 40 base, +20 if the file holds more than 40 characters of content, +20 x the share of up to 3 sampled markdown links that resolve to a working URL (or a flat +10 if the file contains no links at all), +20 if a date appears anywhere in it.
Score capped at 100.
TECH-03.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. File presence, HTTP resolution of the links it lists, and a date pattern are all deterministic checks against a fetched file.

TECH-04.name: No login, pop-up or cookie wall covering main content
TECH-04.definition: Whether the main content is reachable without dismissing a consent banner, modal or login. Crawlers do not click Accept, so anything behind an overlay is effectively invisible to them.
TECH-04.metric_brief: Scan the raw homepage HTML for overlay markers (cookie, consent, GDPR vendors, modal, overlay, paywall) and for a login or password form. 100 when neither is present, 70 when markers exist but 150 or more words are still present, 20 otherwise, and capped at 20 for a login form on a near-empty page.
TECH-04.metric:
Scan the raw homepage HTML for overlay markers (cookie, consent, gdpr, onetrust, cookiebot, trustarc, cookieyes, modal, overlay, paywall) and for a login form or password input.
Score = 100 if neither is present; 70 if markers are present but at least 150 words still survive; 20 otherwise. Capped at 20 when a login form is present and the page yields under 80 words.
Confidence 0.55.
TECH-04.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Decided from DOM markers plus the word count. The low confidence reflects that a marker in the HTML does not prove an overlay actually covers content; proving that needs visual or viewport analysis, not a language model. This build runs no JavaScript, so an overlay that only mounts on the client never reaches the HTML this inspects.

TECH-05.name: Sitemap complete, accurate and submitted
TECH-05.definition: Whether an XML sitemap exists, lists URLs that actually resolve, and covers the pages the site really has. A sitemap is how a crawler finds pages it would not reach by following links.
TECH-05.metric_brief: Read the sitemaps discovered from robots.txt and the well-known locations, fetch the first 15 listed URLs to test that they resolve, and compare the crawled page set against the sitemap. Score is a 25-point base plus weighted validity (45) and coverage (30). 0 when no sitemap is found at all.
TECH-05.metric:
Read the XML sitemap(s) discovered from robots.txt and the well-known locations. Fetch the first 15 sitemap URLs to test whether they resolve, and compare the set of crawled pages against the set of sitemap URLs.
Validity = resolving sampled URLs / sampled URLs x 100.
Coverage = crawled pages that appear in the sitemap / crawled pages x 100.
Score = 25 + Validity x 0.45 + Coverage x 0.30, capped at 100.
Score 0 if no sitemap URLs were found at all.
TECH-05.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. XML parsing, HTTP resolution and set comparison are exact operations.

TECH-06.name: No broken links, redirect chains or error pages
TECH-06.definition: Whether internal links lead somewhere. Broken links and long redirect chains waste crawl budget and break the path an assistant follows to reach supporting content.
TECH-06.metric_brief: Take a deterministic sample of 15 internal links and fetch each one. A link is broken on failure or a non-2xx status, and counts as a chain at 3 or more hops. Score is the share that resolve, less 5 points per chain up to a 20-point maximum.
TECH-06.metric:
Take a deterministic sample of 15 internal links from the crawl and fetch each one. A link is broken if the fetch fails or returns a non-2xx status; it is a redirect chain if it takes 3 or more hops.
Score = (sampled - broken) / sampled x 100 - min(20, chains x 5), floored at 0.
Confidence 0.7.
TECH-06.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. HTTP status codes and redirect hop counts are facts recorded by the fetcher.

TECH-07.name: Page speed and Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS)
TECH-07.definition: How quickly and cheaply a page delivers its content; slow, heavy pages are crawled less often and less completely. This is a latency and page-weight proxy: no Lighthouse or Chromium performance run is wired into this build, so real LCP, INP and CLS are not measured.
TECH-07.metric_brief: Measure server response time and transferred HTML size across up to 12 crawled pages, band each mean into four tiers, and combine as latency x 0.6 plus weight x 0.4. Confidence is held at 0.4 because this is a proxy, not a measured vitals run.
TECH-07.metric:
Measure server response time and transferred HTML size across up to 12 successfully crawled pages, then band each mean:
   Latency:  <=800ms -> 100,  <=1800ms -> 70,  <=3000ms -> 40,  else 20
   Weight:   <=300KB -> 100,  <=800KB  -> 70,  <=1.5MB  -> 40,  else 20
Score = Latency x 0.6 + Weight x 0.4.   Confidence 0.4.
TECH-07.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Timing and byte size are measured directly. The confidence is deliberately low: this is a proxy, not Core Web Vitals. Real LCP, INP and CLS require a rendering or field-data source (Lighthouse or CrUX). That is a missing integration, not something a language model could supply.

TECH-08.name: Mobile responsiveness and secure HTTPS delivery
TECH-08.definition: Whether the site is served over HTTPS and declares a mobile viewport. Both are baseline trust and accessibility signals, and an insecure or non-responsive page is discounted by every major crawler.
TECH-08.metric_brief: 50 points if the homepage's final URL is HTTPS, plus 50 if a viewport meta tag containing width is present. Capped at 80 when the HTML carries a fixed-width layout signal, a weak indication the page may overflow on mobile.
TECH-08.metric:
Score = 50 if the homepage final URL is https, + 50 if a viewport meta tag containing "width" is present.
Capped at 80 if the HTML contains both "min-width:" and "1200px", a weak signal of a fixed-width layout that may overflow on mobile.
TECH-08.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. URL scheme and meta-tag presence are read directly from the response and the DOM.

TECH-09.name: Main content present in page source, not JS-only
TECH-09.definition: Whether the content exists in the HTML the server sends or only appears once JavaScript has run. Many AI crawlers do not execute JavaScript, so client-rendered copy is invisible to them.
TECH-09.metric_brief: Intended to compare the raw pre-JavaScript word count against a JavaScript-rendered one. This build has no browser-rendering pass (httpx + lxml + Crawlee only), so there is no rendered copy to compare against and this parameter always reports UNKNOWN.
TECH-09.metric:
Always UNKNOWN in this build: this check requires comparing raw HTML against a JavaScript-rendered copy of the page, which this build does not fetch (httpx + lxml + Crawlee only, no browser rendering).
Historical formula, for when a rendered copy was available: for each of the first 10 pages, strip <script> and <style> from the RAW HTML, strip the remaining tags, and count the words left; per-page ratio = raw words / rendered words x 100, capped at 100 per page; score = mean of the per-page capped ratios.
TECH-09.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Not evaluated. The comparison needs two versions of the same document and this build produces only one, so the check reports UNKNOWN rather than the meaningless 100 it would score by comparing the raw HTML against itself.

TECH-10.name: One H1 per page and logical H2/H3 hierarchy
TECH-10.definition: Whether headings form a clean, single-rooted outline. The heading tree is how an assistant segments a page into passages it can quote, so a missing or duplicated H1 and skipped levels blur those boundaries.
TECH-10.metric_brief: Per page start at 100, subtract 40 for no H1 or 25 for more than one, and 10 per skipped heading level up to 30. Score is the mean across pages, or 0 outright if no page has any headings.
TECH-10.metric:
Per page, start at 100. Subtract 40 if there is no H1, or 25 if there is more than one. Subtract min(30, skips x 10), where a skip is a jump of more than one heading level between consecutive headings. Floor each page at 0.
Score = mean of per-page scores.
Score 0 outright if no headings were found on any page.
TECH-10.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Counting H1 tags and comparing consecutive heading levels is exact.

TECH-11.name: Heading frequency that lets an assistant lift a clean passage
TECH-11.definition: Whether sections are short and self-contained enough that an assistant can lift one whole as an answer. A two-thousand-word stretch under a single heading offers no clean extraction boundary.
TECH-11.metric_brief: The heuristic penalises a high mean words-per-heading and a low heading density per page. When the model is available it receives up to 40 real heading and section-length pairs and returns how many of those sections an assistant could lift whole; the score is liftable sections over sections assessed.
TECH-11.metric:
Heuristic baseline per page: start at 100, -30 if mean words per heading exceeds 220, -20 if heading density is under 1.5 per 1000 words, or a flat 30 if the page has no H1-H3 at all.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): up to 40 real (heading, word count of the text under that heading up to the next heading) pairs go to the model, which returns how many of those sections an assistant could lift whole.
Score = liftable sections / sections assessed x 100.
TECH-11.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. Whether a section can be lifted as a clean, self-contained passage is a judgment about whether its heading actually scopes its content. Word counts alone cannot distinguish a focused 200-word section from a rambling one of the same length.
The heuristic stays as the fallback when the model is unavailable, so a scan never fails for lack of an API key.

TECH-12.name: Tables and lists as real markup rather than images
TECH-12.definition: Whether comparison and specification content is real HTML markup rather than a screenshot. Text inside an image cannot be read, quoted or cited.
TECH-12.metric_brief: Count <table> elements and <ul>/<ol> elements across every crawled page. 100 at 8 or more combined, 70 at 3 or more, else 40.
TECH-12.metric:
Count <table> elements and <ul>/<ol> elements across every crawled page.
Score = 100 if tables + lists >= 8; 70 if >= 3; else 40.
TECH-12.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Element counting is exact.
Known limitation: this confirms semantic markup exists but does not detect the failure mode in the parameter name - a comparison table published as an image. Catching that needs image analysis (a vision model or OCR), which is not wired into this build.

TECH-13.name: Text-to-code ratio and content depth per page
TECH-13.definition: How much of a page is prose rather than markup and scaffolding, and whether it carries enough substance to answer anything. A thin page wrapped in a heavy template gives an assistant little to work with.
TECH-13.metric_brief: Per page, band the visible-text-to-HTML character ratio into five tiers -- a content-rich page sits near 20-25%, so the raw ratio is not itself a score -- and compute depth against a 400-word target. Per-page score is 40% ratio band plus 60% depth; the score is the mean across pages.
TECH-13.metric:
Per page:
   Text-to-code = visible text characters / total HTML characters x 100, then banded, because a byte ratio is not a score (a content-rich page sits near 20-25% and never approaches 100):
      >=25% -> 100,  >=15% -> 85,  >=10% -> 70,  >=5% -> 45,  else 20
   Depth = min(100, words / 400 x 100)
   Per-page score = banded text-to-code x 0.4 + Depth x 0.6
Score = mean across pages.
TECH-13.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Character ratios and word counts are measured directly from the fetched HTML.

TECH-14.name: Image alt text and video transcripts
TECH-14.definition: Whether non-text media carries a text equivalent. Alt text and transcripts are the only route by which the content of an image or video enters an assistant's index.
TECH-14.metric_brief: Alt text counts as usable when it is non-empty, longer than 3 characters and not a placeholder such as image, img or logo. The image score is the usable share; the video score is transcript signals over video embeds, or 100 where there are no videos. Score is image x 0.7 plus video x 0.3.
TECH-14.metric: Collect every across the crawl. Alt text counts as usable if it is non-empty, longer than 3 characters, and not one of the placeholder values image/img/logo. Count
TECH-14.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Attribute presence and a placeholder blocklist are deterministic.
Known limitation: this measures whether alt text exists and is non-trivial, not whether it actually describes the image. Judging descriptiveness would need a vision model - a deliberate scope boundary, not an oversight.

TECH-15.name: Published and updated dates visible and in code
TECH-15.definition: Whether pages expose when they were published and last changed. Assistants weight recency heavily, and an undated page is treated as being of unknown age.
TECH-15.metric_brief: A page counts as dated if it exposes article:published_time, article:modified_time, a <time> element, or datePublished/dateModified in its JSON-LD. Score is 60 plus 40 times the dated share; the 60 floor reflects that dates matter most on articles, not on home and service pages.
TECH-15.metric:
A page counts as dated if it exposes a published or modified date through article:published_time, article:modified_time or a <time> element, or through datePublished/dateModified in its JSON-LD.
Score = 60 + (dated pages / pages) x 40.
The 60 floor is deliberate: dates matter most on articles, so their absence on home and service pages is treated as partial rather than a total failure.
TECH-15.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Metadata and JSON-LD field presence are read directly.

TECH-16.name: Organization markup — logo, address, contact, profiles
TECH-16.definition: Whether the homepage carries Organization schema naming the company, its logo, contact details and official profiles. This is the record that lets an assistant resolve the site to a real-world entity rather than treat it as loose text.
TECH-16.metric_brief: Find an Organization node in the homepage JSON-LD and check for name, url, logo and sameAs, with address or contact fields as a bonus group. Score is the share of the four expected fields x 80, plus 20 for any address or contact field. 0 if no Organization node exists.
TECH-16.metric:
Find an Organization node in the homepage JSON-LD. Expected fields are name, url, logo and sameAs; address/location and contactPoint/email/telephone count as a bonus group.
Score = (expected fields present / 4) x 80 + 20 if any address or contact field is present.
Score 0 if no Organization node exists.
TECH-16.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Checking for named fields in parsed JSON-LD is exact.

TECH-17.name: Page-type markup — Article, FAQ, Service, Product, Person, HowTo
TECH-17.definition: Whether each page's schema type matches what the page actually is -- Article, Service, Organization and so on. Correct type markup tells an assistant how to read the page instead of inferring it from layout.
TECH-17.metric_brief: Map each detected page type to the schema.org types that genuinely satisfy it, and exclude page types the check does not apply to. Score is matched pages over applicable pages, or 50 when no page is applicable.
TECH-17.metric:
Map each page detected type to the schema.org types that genuinely satisfy it:
   article     -> Article, BlogPosting, NewsArticle, TechArticle, Report
   service     -> Service, Product, Offer, ProfessionalService
   about       -> Organization, Corporation, LocalBusiness, AboutPage
   home        -> Organization, Corporation, LocalBusiness, WebSite
   case_study  -> Article, CaseStudy, CreativeWork
Pages of other types are not applicable and are excluded.
Score = matched pages / applicable pages x 100, or 50 if no page is applicable.
TECH-17.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Matching type strings against an explicit allowlist is deterministic. The allowlist is the point: it replaces a rule that accepted FAQPage as satisfying any expected type, which let a blog post carrying only FAQPage count as correctly marked-up Article content.

TECH-18.name: Author profiles marked up with real credentials
TECH-18.definition: Whether content is attributed in markup to an identifiable person with a stated role. Author identity is a primary expertise signal for anything an assistant treats as advice.
TECH-18.metric_brief: Collect author signals across the crawl: Person nodes or author fields in JSON-LD, plus visible [rel=author], .author or .byline elements. 25 when no signal is found, 80 when any is found, and 95 when an author node also carries a jobTitle.
TECH-18.metric:
Collect author signals across the crawl: Person nodes or author fields in JSON-LD, plus visible [rel=author], .author or .byline elements.
Score = 25 if no signal is found; 80 if any signal is found; 95 if any author node carries a jobTitle.
Confidence 0.65.
TECH-18.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Schema nodes and CSS selectors are read directly.
Known limitation: this confirms an author is named and titled, not that the credentials are real. Verifying that needs external identity sources, not a language model.

TECH-19.name: Markup validates cleanly and matches visible content
TECH-19.definition: Whether the structured data on the site actually parses. Malformed JSON-LD is discarded silently, so a site can carry extensive markup and get no benefit from any of it.
TECH-19.metric_brief: Count every JSON-LD block found across the crawl and how many parsed successfully; the score is the valid share. UNKNOWN when the site has no JSON-LD at all, since whether markup should exist is already scored by TECH-16 and TECH-17.
TECH-19.metric:
Count every JSON-LD block found across the crawl and how many parsed successfully.
Score = valid blocks / total blocks x 100.
UNKNOWN when the site has no JSON-LD at all: nothing to validate is not the same as 40% valid, and whether markup should exist is already scored by TECH-16 and TECH-17.
TECH-19.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. JSON parse success is binary and exact.
Known limitation: the "matches visible content" half of this parameter name is not currently evaluated - only syntactic validity is.

TECH-20.name: One clean URL per page; duplicates resolved
TECH-20.definition: Whether each page has one canonical address. Duplicate URLs for the same content split the signals an assistant uses to decide which version to cite.
TECH-20.metric_brief: Flag a page when it carries no canonical link, when an absolute canonical points at a different path than the page's own final path (the homepage excepted), or when it took 3 or more redirect hops. Score is the share of pages with no problem.
TECH-20.metric:
Per page, flag a problem when: no canonical link is present; or an absolute canonical points to a path that differs from the page own final path (excluding the homepage); or the page took 3 or more redirect hops.
Score = pages with no problem / pages x 100.
TECH-20.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. URL comparison and redirect hop counts are exact.

TECH-21.name: hreflang set correctly for every target country
TECH-21.definition: Whether a multi-market site declares which language and region each page version serves. Without hreflang, assistants can surface the wrong regional page or treat the variants as duplicates.
TECH-21.metric_brief: Collect every <link rel=alternate hreflang> across the crawl; a tag is valid when it carries both a lang and an href, and the score is the valid share. UNKNOWN when none is found: a single-market site is not applicable, so it is excluded from the pillar average rather than passed or failed.
TECH-21.metric:
Collect every <link rel=alternate hreflang> across the crawl.
UNKNOWN when none is found: a single-market site is not applicable to this check, so it is excluded from the pillar average rather than passed or failed.
When tags are present, a tag is valid if it carries both a lang and an href.
Score = valid tags / tags x 100.
TECH-21.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Attribute presence is exact.
Known limitation: reciprocity between pages and the validity of each locale code are not verified.

TECH-22.name: Page titles and meta descriptions present and unique
TECH-22.definition: Whether every page has a title and a meta description, and whether they are distinct from one another. These are the short summaries an assistant reads to decide what a page is about before reading the page itself.
TECH-22.metric_brief: Across the crawl, measure presence of both fields, title uniqueness, description uniqueness, and length quality (a 20-70 character title and a 70-170 character description). Score is presence x 50 plus title uniqueness x 15 plus description uniqueness x 10 plus length quality x 25.
TECH-22.metric:
Across every crawled page, measure four things:
   Presence               = pages with both a title and a meta description / pages
   Title uniqueness       = distinct non-empty titles / non-empty titles
   Description uniqueness = distinct non-empty descriptions / non-empty descriptions
   Length quality         = pages with a 20-70 char title AND a 70-170 char description / pages
Score = Presence x 50 + Title uniqueness x 15 + Description uniqueness x 10 + Length quality x 25.
TECH-22.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. String lengths and set uniqueness are exact measurements.

ON-01.name: Headings phrased as buyer questions
ON-01.definition: Whether headings are written as the questions buyers actually ask rather than as labels. A question heading matches the shape of a prompt, so the section beneath it is far more likely to be retrieved as an answer.
ON-01.metric_brief: Eligible headings are H1-H3 on service, home and case-study pages with at least 3 words that are not bare navigation labels. The heuristic counts interrogative openers and question marks; when available the model reads up to 40 of them and decides which are questions a buyer would actually ask. The resulting share is banded into five tiers; 30 when there are no eligible headings at all.
ON-01.metric:
Eligible headings are H1-H3 on service, home and case-study pages that have at least 3 words and are not a bare navigation label (home, about, services, blog, pricing ...).
Heuristic baseline: a heading counts as a question if it opens with how/what/why/when/where/which/who/can/should/is/are/do/does/will or ends with a question mark.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): up to 40 headings, sampled at a stride across the eligible set so one heading-heavy page cannot fill the sample, go to the model, which decides which are questions a BUYER would actually ask.
Question share = buyer questions / headings assessed, then banded:
   >=33% -> 100,  >=20% -> 85,  >=10% -> 65,  >=3% -> 45,  else 25
Score 30 if the site has no eligible headings at all.
ON-01.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. The parameter asks for headings phrased as the questions buyers ask, which is a statement about intent, not grammar. "What We Do" has interrogative form and no buyer has ever typed it; "Pricing for mid-market teams" has none and answers a question buyers ask constantly. The regex scores both exactly backwards.
The banding is kept either way: a raw share required about 90% of every heading to be a question for full marks - no well-written page does that, so the check could only ever return FAIL.

ON-02.name: Self-contained 40–60 word answer under each question
ON-02.definition: Whether each question heading is followed by a complete answer that stands on its own. An assistant lifts a passage without its surroundings, so an answer that depends on the paragraph before it is unusable.
ON-02.metric_brief: For every question-phrased heading, take the text up to the next heading as the answer. 70 base at 20 or more words, plus 30 in the 40-60 word target window or 15 in a 25-90 word band, capped at 100 per answer. Score is the mean; 25 with a diagnostic when there are no question headings to score.
ON-02.metric:
For every question-phrased H1-H3, take the text between it and the next heading as the answer.
   Base    = 70 if the answer runs to 20 words or more, else 30
   Bonus   = +30 if the answer is 40-60 words (the target window), or +15 if it is 25-90 words
   Per-answer score capped at 100
Score = mean across all answers.
Score 25, with a diagnostic naming the reason, when the site has no question headings to score.
ON-02.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. NO - and this is a known gap, recorded here rather than papered over. Word-count windows are deterministic, but the parameter asks whether the answer is SELF-CONTAINED, which is a comprehension judgment a word count cannot make: a 50-word answer that begins "As mentioned above..." scores full marks today.
The registry previously claimed this parameter was AI-assisted; no prompt was ever written for it. The registry has been corrected to match the code, and this is the highest-value place to add a model pass next.

ON-03.name: Clear definition sentences for every core concept
ON-03.definition: Whether the site plainly defines the concepts it is built around instead of assuming the reader knows them. Definition sentences are the passages assistants quote most readily when asked what something is.
ON-03.metric_brief: Concepts are derived from the site's own navigation and service-page titles, never a fixed keyword list. The heuristic tests a 200-character window around each first mention for a definition pattern; when available the model judges whether that window is a clear, complete definition. Score is concepts defined over concepts assessed.
ON-03.metric:
Derive the core concepts from the site own navigation and service-page titles (never a fixed keyword list - every audited site is a different business).
Heuristic baseline: for each concept, look at a 200-character window around its first mention and test for a definition pattern (concept + is/are/means/refers to/helps).
LLM pass (authoritative when available): the model receives each (concept, surrounding window) pair and decides whether the text gives a clear, complete definition rather than a passing mention.
Score = concepts defined / concepts assessed x 100.   Score 30 if no concept could be derived.
ON-03.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. Whether a passage truly DEFINES a concept or merely mentions it is reading comprehension. The regex recognises exactly one sentence shape and misses every definition written another way, while also passing text that happens to contain "is" near the term.

ON-04.name: Conclusion first, supporting detail after
ON-04.definition: Whether a page states its answer up front rather than building to it. Assistants read from the top and weight the opening heavily, so a page that opens with throat-clearing gives away its best extraction.
ON-04.metric_brief: Take the opening of up to 12 pages: the first two substantial sentences, up to 400 characters. The heuristic bands on whether the opening names a site-specific term and avoids filler openings; when available the model judges whether each opening leads with something concrete. Score is openings leading with substance over openings assessed.
ON-04.metric:
Take the opening (first two substantial sentences, up to 400 characters) of up to 12 pages.
Heuristic baseline: 85 if the opening names a site-specific term and avoids filler openings ("welcome to", "in today's", "we are a leading"), 55 if it names a term but also opens with filler, 35 otherwise.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): the model judges per opening whether it leads with a specific, concrete statement rather than boilerplate.
Score = openings leading with substance / openings assessed x 100.
ON-04.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. "Leads with the conclusion" is a statement about meaning, not vocabulary. A page can open with a brand term and still say nothing, or open with none of the keywords and be perfectly direct.

ON-05.name: FAQ section on every service and solution page
ON-05.definition: Whether service and solution pages carry an FAQ. FAQ blocks are the densest question and answer format on a site and map directly onto the way buyers prompt an assistant.
ON-05.metric_brief: Identify service and solution pages by page type or a service/solution URL. A page qualifies with an FAQ heading or FAQPage schema, and the score is the qualifying share. UNKNOWN when the site has no service or solution pages, since there is nothing for the check to apply to.
ON-05.metric:
Identify service and solution pages (page type service or home, or a URL containing service/solution). A page satisfies the check if it has a heading matching FAQ / frequently asked, or carries FAQPage schema.
Score = qualifying pages / service pages x 100.
UNKNOWN when the site has no service or solution pages, since there is nothing the check applies to.
ON-05.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Heading regex and schema type presence are exact.
The UNKNOWN path replaces a fallback that graded EVERY crawled page when no service page was found, which demanded an FAQ section on contact and careers pages too.

ON-5.1.name: FAQ schema validity and answer consistency
ON-5.1.definition: Whether FAQ content is also marked up as FAQPage structured data, so the questions and answers are machine-readable rather than only visually formatted. The answer-consistency half of this parameter -- whether the schema answers match the visible Q&A -- is semantic and is not currently verified.
ON-5.1.metric_brief: Consider only pages that have FAQ schema or a visible FAQ mention. Award 50 for valid FAQPage JSON-LD and 50 for a visible FAQ, and take the mean across those pages. 20 when neither appears anywhere on the site.
ON-5.1.metric:
Consider only pages that have FAQ schema or a visible FAQ mention.
Per page: 50 if valid FAQPage JSON-LD is present + 50 if a visible FAQ is present.
Score = mean across those pages.   Score 20 if neither appears anywhere on the site.
ON-5.1.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Schema presence and a text match are deterministic.
Known limitation: the "answer consistency" half of the parameter - whether the schema answers match the visible Q&A - is not verified. That comparison is semantic and would need a model.

ON-07.name: Comparison and specification tables where buyers evaluate
ON-07.definition: Whether pages where a buyer is actively comparing options present that comparison as a real table. A table is the cleanest structure for an assistant to read attribute-by-attribute differences from.
ON-07.metric_brief: The heuristic marks a page as evaluation-intent on vs, compare, alternative, pricing, feature or capability signals, or on being a service page. When available the model decides which pages are genuinely evaluation pages -- it sets the denominator -- while the numerator stays the measured fact of whether a real HTML table exists. 40 when none qualify.
ON-07.metric:
Heuristic baseline: a page shows evaluation intent if its title, opening text or URL contains vs / compar / alternative / pricing / feature / capability, or it is a service page.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): a page-type-spread sample of 24 pages goes to the model, which decides which are pages where a buyer is actively evaluating or comparing options. The numerator stays the measured fact - does that page carry a real HTML <table>.
Score = evaluation pages with a table / evaluation pages x 100.   Score 40 if none qualify.
ON-07.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. Which pages are evaluation pages is a judgment about purpose: a pricing page qualifies without containing "vs", and a blog post titled "X vs Y" often does not. The keyword list both over- and under-selects, and it sets the DENOMINATOR, so getting it wrong skews the whole score.

ON-08.name: Lists and numbered steps that support answer extraction
ON-08.definition: Whether lists carry real procedural or evaluative content rather than acting as decoration. A genuine step or criteria list is directly liftable as a structured answer.
ON-08.metric_brief: Collect <ul>/<ol> with 2 or more items that sit outside nav, header and footer, so repeated menus are excluded. The heuristic marks a list useful at 3 or more items mentioning step, how, benefit, includes, deliver or process; when available the model judges genuine usefulness across up to 30 lists. 35 when no content lists exist.
ON-08.metric:
Collect content lists - <ul>/<ol> with 2 or more items that are not inside <nav>, <header> or <footer>, so repeated menus are excluded.
Heuristic baseline: a list is useful if it has 3 or more items and mentions step/how/benefit/includ/deliver/process.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): up to 30 lists go to the model, which judges whether each is genuinely useful for answering a question rather than decorative filler.
Score = useful lists / lists assessed x 100.   Score 35 if no content lists exist.
ON-08.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. Usefulness of a list is a reading judgment. The keyword test only recognises a list that happens to contain one of six words, so it misses a genuine specification or evaluation-criteria list written without them.

ON-10.name: Keyword stuffing / unnatural repetition
ON-10.definition: Whether copy repeats one term far beyond what natural prose does. Heavy repetition reads as manipulation and degrades the quality of any passage lifted from the page.
ON-10.metric_brief: For each page with 40 or more content words, compute the density of its single most frequent content word, then average across pages and band at under 3.5% to 100, under 6% to 75, else 45. Function words are removed first, without which "the" would be the peak term on almost every English page. UNKNOWN if no page has enough copy.
ON-10.metric:
Peak single CONTENT-word density per page (function words removed), averaged across pages, banded:
   <3.5% -> 100,  <6% -> 75,  else 45
UNKNOWN if no page has at least 40 content words.
ON-10.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. NO, deliberately. Keyword stuffing is a measurable statistical property, so the check is kept fully deterministic and reproducible: it cannot drift with model behaviour.
The stopword filter is what makes it work at all. Counting function words made "the" the peak term on essentially every English page at 4-7%, which sat above the worst band - so every site scored the same floor and the check reported nothing.

ON-11.name: Content depth and completeness
ON-11.definition: Whether a service page actually covers what a buyer needs in order to decide, or only asserts that it does. A gap in coverage is where an assistant turns to a competitor's page to complete the answer.
ON-11.metric_brief: The rubric is 8 points a complete service page should cover: problem, approach, what is included, outcomes, who it is for, commercial model, proof and next step. The heuristic tests keyword presence; when available the model counts how many points each page actually covers across a 12-page spread. Score is the mean of points covered over 8.
ON-11.metric:
The rubric is 8 points a complete service page should cover: problem/need, approach or methodology, what is included, outcomes or benefits, who it is for, pricing or commercial model, proof, and a clear next step.
Heuristic baseline: keyword presence per rubric point.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): excerpts from a page-type-spread sample of 12 pages go to the model, which counts how many rubric points each page ACTUALLY covers. The denominator is unchanged - the same pages, out of the same 8 points.
Score = mean(points covered / 8) x 100.
ON-11.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. Whether a page really covers "outcomes" or "proof" is comprehension, not keyword presence. A case study that describes a measured result covers "outcomes" without using the word; a page with a "Benefits" heading and no substance does not.

ON-12.name: Original, citable data point on major pages
ON-12.definition: Whether important pages carry a concrete statistic worth citing. A specific number is what makes a page quotable rather than merely paraphrasable.
ON-12.metric_brief: Major pages are home, service, case-study and about pages, not every blog post. A statistic is a percentage, an N+ figure, a currency amount, a multiplier or a scaled number; bare four-digit years are excluded so a copyright line does not count. The heuristic scores the share of major pages carrying one; when available the model judges whether those statistics are original to the company rather than quoted, and that rate scales the score.
ON-12.metric:
Major pages are home, service, case-study and about pages (not every blog post).
A statistic is a percentage, an N+ figure, a currency amount, a multiplier (3x), a thousands-separated number, or a scaled figure (2.5 million). Bare four-digit years are explicitly excluded.
Heuristic baseline: Score = major pages carrying at least one statistic / major pages x 100.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): up to 24 major pages that carry a statistic go to the model with their figures and an excerpt, and it decides whether at least one of them is ORIGINAL to this company rather than quoted off a third party.
Score = (major pages with a statistic / major pages) x (pages judged original / pages assessed) x 100, so the denominator stays every major page and only the numerator moves.
ON-12.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. The pattern establishes that a statistic is PRESENT; the parameter asks for an ORIGINAL, citable one. A figure quoted off an analyst firm satisfies the regex and fails the parameter, and telling the two apart means reading the sentence around the number.
The pattern itself stays deterministic and is the other half of the fix: the previous rule matched any 2+ digit number, so a copyright year, street number or phone fragment satisfied "has an original statistic".

ON-13.name: Named author with role, credentials and real profile
ON-13.definition: Whether content carries a named author with a stated role and a real profile. This is the on-page half of the expertise signal that TECH-18 checks in markup. The linked profile is not fetched, so that the person is real and reachable is still not independently verified.
ON-13.metric_brief: Collect visible [rel=author], .author or .byline elements and Person nodes in JSON-LD, keeping the byline text. Without the model, 80 if any author signal exists anywhere, else 30. With it, up to 20 bylines are read and scored half for naming a real person and half for stating that person's role, floored at 30.
ON-13.metric:
Collect visible [rel=author], .author or .byline elements and Person nodes in JSON-LD across the crawl, capturing the byline TEXT rather than only the fact that an element matched.
Heuristic baseline: Score = 80 if any author signal exists anywhere, else 30.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): up to 20 bylines go to the model, which decides for each whether it names a specific real person - not a company, and not a generic label such as "Admin" or "Editorial Team" - and whether it states that person's role or credentials.
Score = named people / assessed x 50 + named people who also state a role / assessed x 50, floored at 30: markup that names nobody is no worse than no markup at all.
ON-13.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. The selector proves a byline element exists, which is not what the parameter asks for. "Posted by Admin" and "Dr Jane Roe, Principal Data Engineer" both match it and are not remotely the same expertise signal; separating them means reading the text.
Known limitation that remains: the linked profile is still not fetched to confirm the person is real and reachable. That is a data-collection gap, not a judgment a model can close.

ON-14.name: Named clients, quantified outcomes, deployment detail
ON-14.definition: Whether case-study and proof content names who the work was for, what it measurably achieved and how it was delivered. An unattributed claim is not citable evidence.
ON-14.metric_brief: The rubric is 25 for a client mention, 30 for a quantified figure, 25 for deployment language, and a 20 bonus when both appear. The heuristic applies it by regex across all pages; when available the model applies the same rubric by reading a 20-page spread, deciding whether a specific client is actually named rather than the generic word used.
ON-14.metric:
Heuristic baseline, per page: 25 if the copy mentions a client/customer/partner, + 30 if it contains a quantified figure, + 25 if it describes deployment (deploy/implementation/production/rolled out), + 20 bonus when both a client mention and a figure are present. Score = mean across pages.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): a page-type-spread sample of 20 pages goes to the model, which judges the same three signals by reading them - does the page NAME a specific client organisation, is the outcome genuinely quantified, is deployment actually described.
Score = mean of the same 25/30/25/+20 rubric applied to the model's verdicts, so the rubric is unchanged and only the reading of each signal improves.
ON-14.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. The regex cannot distinguish a NAMED client from the generic word "client", which is precisely what the parameter asks for, and it counts any two-digit number as a quantified outcome - so a phone number or a street number scores the same as a measured result.

ON-15.name: Claims sourced and dated to a primary source
ON-15.definition: Whether factual claims sit next to a citation. An unsourced statistic is a claim an assistant has no reason to repeat. Without the model the check establishes only that something source-like sits near the claim, not that a reader could check it.
ON-15.metric_brief: A claim is a sentence of more than 6 words containing a statistic, using the ON-12 pattern with years excluded. The heuristic counts a claim as sourced on nearby link anchor text or the words source, according to, or report; when available the model reads up to 24 claims and decides which are attributed to a source a reader could actually check. 35 when no claims are found.
ON-15.metric:
A claim is a sentence of more than 6 words containing a statistic (same pattern as ON-12, years excluded).
Heuristic baseline: a claim counts as sourced if the sentence contains link anchor text from that page, or the words source / according to / report. Score = sourced claims / claims x 100.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): up to 24 claims go to the model together with any adjacent link anchor text, and it decides whether each is attributed to a source a reader could actually check - a named organisation, publication, study or dated report.
Score = attributed claims / claims assessed x 100.   Score 35 if no claims were found.
ON-15.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. The regex establishes only that something source-LIKE sits near the claim: the bare word "report" anywhere in the sentence satisfies it, as does a link whose anchor text happens to appear in the text. Whether the source is identifiable and checkable - which is the parameter - requires reading the sentence.

ON-17.name: Last substantive update within topic shelf life
ON-17.definition: Whether pages show they have been kept current. Stale content is discounted, and on fast-moving topics it is actively misleading. The check measures date presence only: no age comparison against topic shelf life is made, so a page dated 2009 scores as a page dated last week.
ON-17.metric_brief: Score is 50 plus 50 times the share of pages exposing a published or modified date.
ON-17.metric:
Score = 50 + (pages exposing a published or modified date / pages) x 50.
Confidence 0.6.
ON-17.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: no. Date metadata presence is exact.
Known limitation: the parameter asks for updates WITHIN TOPIC SHELF LIFE, and no age comparison is made at all - a page dated 2009 scores exactly like one dated last week. Closing that needs date arithmetic plus a per-topic shelf-life judgment, not just presence.

ON-18.name: Buying-journey coverage across discovery to decision
ON-18.definition: Whether the site has content for every stage a buyer moves through, not only the bottom of the funnel. A missing stage is a point at which the buyer's question gets answered by somebody else.
ON-18.metric_brief: The six stages are awareness, qualification, comparison, objection, trust and decision. The heuristic keyword-matches page titles, opening text and URLs; when available the model reads the titles and URLs of a 60-page spread and decides which stages have content. Score is stages covered over 6.
ON-18.metric:
The six buyer-journey stages are awareness, qualification, comparison, objection, trust and decision.
Heuristic baseline: keyword matching over each page title, opening text and URL.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): the titles and URLs of a page-type-spread sample of 60 pages go to the model, which decides which of the six stages the site has content for.
Score = stages covered / 6 x 100.
ON-18.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. What stage a page serves is a judgment about purpose. A pricing page aids comparison whether or not it contains the word "vs"; a security page handles objections without using the word "objection".

ON-19.name: Best X for Y and X vs Y pages per industry/market
ON-19.definition: Whether the site has pages built for the high-intent comparison queries buyers actually run. These are the queries an assistant is most often asked to answer directly. Whether those pages cover the specific industries and markets that matter to this business is not measured -- that needs a target list the audit is not given.
ON-19.metric_brief: The heuristic matches page URLs and titles against best ... for, vs, versus and alternative; when available the model reads the titles and URLs of a 30-page spread and decides which genuinely serve a high-intent comparison query. 80 at 3 or more such pages, 45 at one or more, else 15.
ON-19.metric:
Heuristic baseline: match each page URL and title against best ... for / vs / versus / alternative.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): the titles and URLs of a page-type-spread sample of 30 pages go to the model, which decides which are genuinely built to answer a high-intent comparison query rather than merely containing the words.
Score = 80 if 3 or more such pages are found; 45 if at least one; else 15.
ON-19.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. The token match both over- and under-selects, and it is the whole measurement. A blog post titled "Docker vs Podman" matches and is not a buyer comparison page; "Choosing an ERP for manufacturers" is one and matches nothing. Which pages serve a high-intent comparison query is a judgment about purpose.
Known limitation that remains: this counts whether such pages EXIST, not whether they cover the industries and markets that matter to this business - that needs a target list the audit is not given.

ON-20.name: No two pages competing for the same question (cannibalization)

ON-20.metric_brief: Title token sets are compared by Jaccard similarity to find candidate pairs at 0.7 or above; an exact prefix filter gives a result identical to comparing every pair but runs in seconds at the 2,500-page crawl ceiling. ON-20.metric:
Compare page titles as token sets (4+ character tokens) using Jaccard similarity. Two pages are CANDIDATES to compete when similarity >= 0.7 and the titles are not identical strings.
Comparison uses an exact prefix filter, not all pairs, so the result is identical to comparing every pair but runs in seconds at the 2500-page crawl ceiling.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): up to 20 candidate pairs go to the model, which confirms which of them really answer the same buyer question. Unconfirmed pairs stop counting against the site; candidates past the sample keep their heuristic verdict rather than being silently dropped.
Clean share = 1 - (pages in a competing pair / pages compared), then banded:
   100% -> 100,  >=95% -> 90,  >=85% -> 75,  >=70% -> 60,  else 40
UNKNOWN if no page has a title.

Scored by the model. When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

A service page and the case study about that service share most of their tokens without competing, and so does the same service written for two different industries. Whether two pages really compete for one buyer question is a judgment the similarity score cannot make, and it sets the whole penalty.
The model only ever narrows the candidate set, so the check cannot invent cannibalisation that the deterministic filter did not find.
Banding by share rather than a flat penalty per pair stays: 12 points per pair meant nine overlapping titles bottomed out the check whether the site had 20 pages or 2000.

Thin pages are non-utility pages under 180 words. Near-duplicates are pages whose first 400 characters overlap at Jaccard >= 0.72, found with the same exact prefix filter as ON-20.

OFF-18.name: Analyst, directory and trade-press coverage + description accuracy
OFF-18.definition: Whether analysts and trade press cover the company, and whether what they say about it is correct. An inaccurate third-party description is worse than none, because it propagates.
OFF-18.metric_brief: Search for the company name with gartner, forrester, idc, analyst report or industry report, and extract result titles and snippets. The heuristic scores 55 when snippets are returned and 20 when none are; when available the model judges whether they describe this company accurately. 80 if accurate, 40 if not.
OFF-18.metric:
DuckDuckGo HTML search for the company name together with gartner / forrester / idc / analyst report / industry report; extract result titles and snippets.
Heuristic baseline: 55 when any snippets are returned, 20 when none are.
LLM pass (authoritative when available): the model judges whether the snippets describe THIS company accurately, rather than confusing it with another or repeating outdated facts.
Score = 80 if accurate, 40 if not.   Confidence 0.55 with the model, 0.35 without.
OFF-18.llm_rationale:
Scored by the model. The curated data this parameter extracts is sent to the model together with this parameter's definition and metric, and the model returns the score, the explanation and the recommendation that reach the report (backend/app/parameters/engine.py). When the model is unavailable the rules-based score described below stands in, and the report marks the row as such.

Dedicated pre-scoring model pass: yes. YES. Detecting a snippet that describes a different company with a similar name, or repeats a stale fact, requires reading and understanding the text. Counting results can only establish that coverage exists, not that it is correct - and "description accuracy" is half the parameter.
